title.es: Tan grande, un problema tan serio

es: Reconocer cuándo usar so (adjetivo solo) y such (con sustantivo) al describir problemas de contaminación.

teaching.en: The river is so dirty that nobody swims in it.
teaching.es: El río está tan sucio que nadie nada en él.
teaching.explanationEs: So + adjetivo solo (dirty); that introduce el resultado.

teaching.en: It is such a serious problem that the city must act.
teaching.es: Es un problema tan serio que la ciudad debe actuar.

teaching.en: We found such dirty plastic bags on the beach.

teaching.explanationEs: Con un sustantivo plural, such va sin a.

teaching.en: It is such bad pollution that we cannot open the windows.

es: Usar so, such, too y enough con that y to + verbo para expresar grado y resultado en problemas del agua y del calor.

teaching.en: The tap water is too dirty to drink.

teaching.en: The heat is so strong that the children stay inside.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo respondes con educación a la objeción de Carlos?

choices.text: That is true, but the club has enough money.
That is true, so the club has enough money.
That is true because the club has enough money.

feedback.es: Se reconoce la objeción y se contrasta con but: That is true, but…

hint.es: Reconoce la objeción y contrasta con una palabra que signifique «pero».

origin.text: Carlos: Bags are too expensive for the club.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estoy de acuerdo con tu propuesta: es un buen plan.»

accepted: agree

feedback.es: Agree es un verbo: I agree with… Sin be.

hint.es: En inglés no se dice «I am ___»: el verbo va solo.

origin.text: I ___ with your proposal: it is a good plan.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tenemos voluntarios suficientes para limpiar el parque.»

answer.text: We have enough volunteers to clean the park.

feedback.es: Enough va antes del sustantivo volunteers, y to + verbo da el objetivo.

hint.es: Enough se coloca delante de volunteers.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es un problema tan serio que necesitamos una votación.»

accepted: such

feedback.es: Con a serious problem (adjetivo + sustantivo singular) se usa such a… that.

origin.text: It is ___ a serious problem that we need a vote.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase dice «El parque no es lo bastante limpio para jugar»?

choices.text: The park is not enough clean to play in.
The park is not clean enough to play in.
The park is not too clean to play in.

feedback.es: Not + adjetivo + enough: enough va después del adjetivo.

prompt.es: Escribe tu propuesta: limpiamos el parque todos los sábados.

answer.text: My proposal is to clean the park every Saturday.
accepted: My proposal is to clean the park every Saturday.
My proposal is that we clean the park every Saturday.
I suggest cleaning the park every Saturday.

feedback.es: Una propuesta clara empieza con My proposal is… o I suggest… y dice qué y cuándo.

origin.text: Propuesta: limpiamos el parque (park) todos los sábados.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué el trabajo será barato.

choices.text: The club will pay many workers.
The club will ask the council for money.
Volunteers will do the work, so it will cost little.

feedback.es: Enough volunteers significa que hay gente suficiente para hacer el trabajo, así que cuesta poco.

origin.audio: Some neighbours are worried about the cost. However, the club has enough volunteers, so the work will be cheap.

prompt.es: Según el discurso, ¿qué pasa con las tiendas por la playa sucia?

choices.text: They have fewer visitors.
They are too expensive.
They close every Sunday.

feedback.es: Tras «As a result» el texto dice que las tiendas tienen menos visitantes.

origin.text: The beach is so dirty that families go to another place. As a result, the shops near the beach have fewer visitors. The club will clean the beach every month if the council gives bags.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tenemos voluntarios suficientes para recoger la basura.»

accepted: enough

feedback.es: Enough va antes del sustantivo: enough volunteers.

origin.text: We have ___ volunteers to collect the litter.

prompt.es: Responde al vecino: objeción, razón con so o such y propuesta para votar.

answer.text: I understand your objection, but we have enough volunteers, so the cost is low. The river is so dirty that children cannot play there. It is such a serious problem that we must act. My proposal is to clean the river every Saturday. Do you agree? Please vote today.
accepted: I understand your objection, but we have enough volunteers, so the cost is low. The river is so dirty that children cannot play there. It is such a serious problem that we must act. My proposal is to clean the river every Saturday. Do you agree? Please vote today.

That is true, but we have enough volunteers, so it will not cost much. The river is so dirty that families do not go there. As a result, the shops have fewer visitors. I suggest cleaning the river every Saturday. Please vote for my proposal today.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta reconoce la objeción, responde con but + enough, da la razón con so o such y termina con una propuesta clara.

origin.text: Vecino: «Es demasiado caro para nuestro barrio.» Reconoce la objeción y di que hay voluntarios suficientes. Explica el problema del río con so o such y propón limpiarlo cada sábado. Pide el voto.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué proponen los vecinos.

choices.text: They want a bigger festival in Green Park.
They want to use another place for the festival.
They want to cancel the festival.

feedback.es: Los vecinos sugieren el patio del colegio porque el parque es demasiado pequeño.

origin.audio: Green Park is too small for the festival, so the neighbours suggest using the school yard.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase expresa causa y resultado con la estructura correcta?

choices.text: The rubbish smells such bad that nobody walks there.
The rubbish smells too bad that nobody walks there.
The rubbish smells so bad that nobody walks there.

feedback.es: So + adjetivo/adverbio + that expresa el resultado; such necesita sustantivo y too pide to.

prompt.es: Cierra tu discurso: pide a los vecinos que apoyen tu propuesta y voten hoy.

answer.text: Do you agree with my proposal? Then please vote today.
accepted: Do you agree with my proposal? Then please vote today.
Please vote for my proposal today.
If you agree with my proposal, please vote today.
Please vote today if you agree with my proposal.

feedback.es: El cierre pide una acción concreta con please: votar hoy si se está de acuerdo con la propuesta.

origin.text: Cierre: pide a los vecinos que estén de acuerdo con tu propuesta y que voten hoy.
